title: US vs UK Fluid Ounces: Why Recipe Conversions Silently Fail
h1: US vs UK fluid ounces — the recipe conversion trap
description: 1 US fl oz = 29.57 mL. 1 UK (Imperial) fl oz = 28.41 mL. Close, but pint sizes diverge 20%. Recipes assume one system.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: US fluid ounce is 4% larger than UK's. But a US pint is 16 fl oz; a UK pint is 20 fl oz. So US pint (473 mL) is 20% smaller than UK pint (568 mL).
body: The single most confusing everyday unit family in English measures. US and UK fluid ounces are close in size, but the numbers of ounces in higher units differ, producing a 20% divergence in pints, quarts and gallons.

> 1 US fl oz = 29.5735 mL
> 1 UK (Imperial) fl oz = 28.4131 mL
> 1 US pint = 16 US fl oz = 473.176 mL
> 1 UK pint = 20 UK fl oz = 568.261 mL
> 1 US gal = 3.785 L; 1 UK gal = 4.546 L (20% larger)
Cocktail recipes (US convention). Beer serving sizes (UK pint on tap in UK, US pint elsewhere). Auto fluid capacities in older UK spec sheets. Baking recipes crossing the Atlantic.

US recipe: 2 cups milk = 16 fl oz = 473 mL. UK cook reads '16 fl oz' and pours 16 Imperial fl oz = 455 mL. Off by 4% — enough to shift batter viscosity on a delicate recipe. Doubled to 1 gallon, the error is 761 mL — the difference between filling a jug and overflowing.
US fl oz ≈ UK fl oz. But everything above (pint, quart, gallon) diverges 20% because the unit ratios differ.

faqs.a: US 'cup' = 8 US fl oz = 237 mL. Metric 'cup' = 250 mL. UK 'cup' historically 10 UK fl oz = 284 mL (rarely used in modern UK recipes).

faqs.q: Are UK litres and US litres the same?
faqs.a: Yes — the litre is universal (1 L = 1000 mL exactly).
